es: Sostener una charla de ocho turnos con preguntas de seguimiento, ecos y una aportación personal equilibrada.

teaching.en: A follow-up question invites the other person to elaborate on one detail.
teaching.es: Una pregunta de seguimiento invita al otro a ampliar un detalle.
teaching.explanationEs: Elaborate = dar más detalles; la pregunta recoge algo que ya dijo.
segments: A follow-up question invites the other
person to elaborate on one detail.
teaching.audioText: A follow-up question invites the other person to elaborate on one detail.

teaching.en: Do not pry: 'How much do you earn?' is too personal for a first chat.
teaching.es: No fisgonees: «¿Cuánto ganas?» es demasiado personal para una primera charla.
teaching.explanationEs: Pry es preguntar cosas demasiado privadas; evita dinero, edad y política.
segments: Do not pry: 'How much do you earn?'
is too personal for a first chat.
teaching.audioText: Do not pry: 'How much do you earn?' is too personal for a first chat.

teaching.en: When she shares something, reciprocate with something of a similar size about yourself.
teaching.es: Cuando ella comparte algo, corresponde con algo de tamaño parecido sobre ti.
teaching.explanationEs: Reciprocate mantiene el equilibrio: ni solo escuchas ni solo hablas.
segments: When she shares something, reciprocate with something
of a similar size about yourself.
teaching.audioText: When she shares something, reciprocate with something of a similar size about yourself.

teaching.en: If you ramble for a minute, the other person can only nod and wait.
teaching.es: Si divagas durante un minuto, el otro solo puede asentir y esperar.
teaching.explanationEs: Ramble es hablar sin un punto claro; dos o tres frases bastan por turno.
segments: If you ramble for a minute, the
other person can only nod and wait.
teaching.audioText: If you ramble for a minute, the other person can only nod and wait.

teaching.en: A short tangent is fine, but return to the thread: 'Anyway, you were telling me about Manta.'
teaching.es: Una digresión breve está bien, pero vuelve al hilo: «En fin, me estabas contando lo de Manta».
teaching.explanationEs: Tangent es salirse del tema; «Anyway, you were saying…» te devuelve a él.
segments: A short tangent is fine, but return to the
thread: 'Anyway, you were telling me about Manta.'

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es una buena pregunta de seguimiento a «I grew up by the sea»?

choices.text: Where is the bathroom?
What was that like?
Do you earn a lot?

feedback.es: Recoge el detalle del mar y pide que el otro lo amplíe.

hint.es: Debe aprovechar el detalle que acaba de decir.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando ella comparte algo, tú correspondes con algo parecido sobre ti.»

feedback.es: Reciprocate es corresponder con una aportación de tamaño parecido.

hint.es: Es el verbo de devolver el gesto.

origin.text: When she shares something, you ___ with something similar about yourself.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Dijiste que fuiste a Lima, ¿cómo fue?»

answer.text: You said you went to Lima what was it like

feedback.es: Se cita el detalle mencionado y después se pregunta.

prompt.es: Elige la pregunta que sería indiscreta con un desconocido.

choices.text: What do you do for a living?
How do you know the bride?
How much did your wedding dress cost?

feedback.es: Preguntar por dinero a un desconocido es indiscreto; las otras dos son preguntas habituales.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el hablante para mantener la charla.

choices.text: He shares a detail and then asks a question.
He gives a long speech about money.
He changes the subject twice.

feedback.es: Cuenta algo breve de sí mismo y devuelve la palabra con una pregunta.

origin.audio: I run a small theatre. Last year we performed in a cave, and it was freezing. Have you ever done anything like that?

prompt.es: Completa: «Estoy acostumbrado a hablar mucho en las fiestas.»

feedback.es: Después de «be used to» va el gerundio: talking.

origin.text: I'm used to ___ a lot at parties, so I try to listen more.

choices.text: Quito. I moved to three cities last year and I will describe each one in detail.
Oh, Quito? I moved cities last year too. What do you miss most?
Oh. Do you like it there?

feedback.es: Corresponde con un dato breve y devuelve una pregunta; el mensaje largo divaga y el corto no aporta nada.

origin.text: I've just moved to Quito for work.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide qué combina el oyente en su turno.

choices.text: An echo and a long story about herself.
A personal note but no question.
An echo, a short personal note and a follow-up question.

feedback.es: Hace un eco, añade una nota personal de una frase y pregunta por los detalles.

origin.audio: You used to sing in a choir? That's great! I tried once, but I was terrible. What kind of songs did you sing?

prompt.es: Completa: «Dijiste que creciste en Cuenca, ¿cómo fue?»

feedback.es: «Grew up» es el pasado de «grow up» y cita el detalle del otro.

origin.text: You said you ___ in Cuenca, what was that like?

prompt.es: Escribe una conversación de ocho turnos en una boda con dos preguntas de seguimiento.

answer.text: Mia: So, how do you know the bride? Leo: We studied together. And you? Mia: I'm her cousin. You studied engineering? Leo: Yes, and I run marathons to relax. What was it like growing up in Manta? Mia: Loud and salty. I play the guitar on the beach. Do you run near Quito? Leo: Every morning, up in the hills. How did you start the guitar? Mia: My grandfather taught me, badly! Shall we find the cake? Leo: Great idea.
accepted: Mia: So, how do you know the bride? Leo: We studied together. And you? Mia: I'm her cousin. You studied engineering? Leo: Yes, and I run marathons to relax. What was it like growing up in Manta? Mia: Loud and salty. I play the guitar on the beach. Do you run near Quito? Leo: Every morning, up in the hills. How did you start the guitar? Mia: My grandfather taught me, badly! Shall we find the cake? Leo: Great idea.

Mia: How do you know the bride? Leo: We worked together. You? Mia: She's my cousin. You work in engineering? Leo: I'm an engineer, and I run marathons on weekends. You grew up in Manta, didn't you? What was that like? Mia: Beautiful. I play the guitar by the sea. Do you run in Quito? Leo: Yes, in the hills. How did you learn the guitar? Mia: My grandfather taught me! Shall we go and eat some cake? Leo: Sure, let's go.

feedback.es: La conversación alterna eco, aportación breve y preguntas de seguimiento sobre detalles que cada uno mencionó.

origin.text: Datos: Mia (enfermera, creció en Manta, toca la guitarra) y Leo (ingeniero, vive en Quito, corre maratones). Incluye un eco y una aportación personal breve de cada uno.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que devuelve el hilo tras una digresión.

choices.text: Anyway, you were telling me about Manta.
By the way, I also like pizza.
Well, that is another story.

feedback.es: «Anyway, you were saying…» vuelve al tema principal; las otras se alejan más.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide cómo reequilibra el hablante la charla.

choices.text: He asks a prying question about money.
He apologises for rambling and hands the turn back.
He ends the chat and leaves.

feedback.es: Se disculpa por haber hablado tanto y devuelve el turno con una pregunta.

origin.audio: Sorry, I've been talking for ages. Enough about me! What about your trip to Japan?

prompt.es: Relaciona cada palabra con su significado en una charla.

feedback.es: Cada palabra describe un movimiento de la charla: preguntar de más, hablar sin punto, dar más detalles o salirse del tema.
